AllPackage.name: North Sikkim Trail
AllPackage.description:
Sikkim has a way of getting to you, in the most delightful sense.

A land where ancient monasteries cling to misty hillsides, colourful festivals fill the mountain air with energy and devotion, and mystic rituals connect you to a way of life that has remained beautifully unchanged for centuries.This travel package, encompassing Gangtok, Lachen, and Lachung, expertly weaves together the most remarkable destinations in this remarkable state, crafting a journey that's both seamless and thoughtfully curated.

From the unspoiled beauty of high-altitude vistas to the serpentine mountain roads, this trip offers a daily dose of genuine adventure, showcasing some of the most breathtaking scenery the Himalayas have to offer. The sheer thrill of the road trips themselves is a feeling that's difficult to put into words until you've lived it.

As you journey, you'll breathe in the crisp mountain air, wander through bustling, age-old bazaars alive with local activity, and marvel at stunning monuments and revered religious sites.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Discover mystic Sikkim on this carefully crafted Gangtok, Lachen, and Lachung package. From breathtaking mountain scenery and ancient bazaars to sacred monasteries and stunning high altitude landscapes, every moment is worth cherishing.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Scenic Himalayan village beside a flowing river with colorful houses and snow-covered mountains in the background, Sikkim.
exclusions: Personal expenses (heater, laundry, calls, tips, water, drinks, entry fees).
Extra sightseeing or additional vehicle usage.
Costs due to landslides, road blocks, or political disturbances (payable on the spot).

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) – Gangtok (130 km / 4 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities: Your adventure kicks off the moment you step out at NJP Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport, where our representative will be right there to greet you and take you on a scenic drive up to Gangtok. The capital city has a way of welcoming every kind of traveller, whether you are chasing peace and quiet or looking for a little thrill. Sitting at 5,480 feet, it holds its place as one of the most visited destinations in the entire country, and it is easy to see why. The drive itself is a treat, with rhododendrons, orchids and delicate colourful butterflies keeping you company along the way. Once you reach the hotel, check in, put your feet up and let yourself breathe. The rest of the day is entirely yours to do as you please. When evening comes around, make your way to MG Marg, a lively and well loved marketplace where you can wander at your own pace and pick up some wonderful things to take back home. Keep an eye out for Thankas, Nepalese dresses, Tibetan carpets, bamboo and cane crafts, alpine cheese, hand woven jackets and even some electronics. Head back to the hotel when you are ready and settle in for a comfortable night in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok (Tsomgo Lake Excursion and Baba Mandir)
activities:
The second day begins with a good breakfast at the hotel before heading out for a day that is going to stay with you for a long time. Today takes you to two of the most remarkable spots around Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake and Baba Harbhajan Mandir.

The Tsomgo Lake

Tsomgo Lake is held as a sacred place by the locals, and spending even a little time here makes it easy to understand why. A small temple sits quietly at its bank, adding to the spiritual feeling of the place. A gorgeous three hour drive takes you up to 12,400 feet where this glacial lake sits in all its glory, ready to take your breath away. What makes it even more special is how the surface of the lake shifts and reflects different colours as the seasons change.

Baba Harbhajan Mandir

Baba Harbhajan Mandir carries a story that is both moving and deeply fascinating. It was built in memory of an Indian soldier who lost his life drowning in a nearby stream, and locals believe his spirit still watches over the Nathula border that connects India to China. Perched at 13,200 feet, the views from up here are nothing short of spectacular. You can also hop on a colourfully decorated yak or pony for a fun little ride around the area.

Optional Tour to Nathula Pass / Additional Charges / Special Permit If you are up for it, a visit to Nathula Pass can also be arranged separately. Walk down the staircase that leads right to the fenced Indo-China border and take in the sheer weight of the moment. Head back to the hotel in Gangtok afterward for a well earned and restful overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – Lachen (125 Km / 6 Hours Approximately)
activities:
Start the morning with a filling breakfast, check out of the hotel in Gangtok and get ready for a drive that is going to be quite something. Lachen is a deep, sweeping valley cradled by towering snow capped mountains that have a way of making you feel very small in the most wonderful sense. It is a quiet and unhurried little hamlet with a small population, and that peaceful quality is a big part of what makes it so appealing. The drive there winds through hot springs and open meadows, and if you keep your eyes open, you might just catch a glimpse of rare birds like the wood snipe or the hoary throated barwing. On arriving, check in at the hotel and head out to take in the surroundings.

Lepcha Village A visit to the Lepcha Village is a chance to step into something genuinely real and unhurried. You get to meet the indigenous people of Sikkim, hear their stories and get a honest feel for what everyday life looks like in a rural corner of this beautiful state. For those who like to get a little more active, the area also opens up into a lovely trekking destination with opportunities for hiking and angling along the way. Head back to the hotel when the day winds down and enjoy a peaceful overnight stay in Lachen.

itinerary.title: Lachen – Gurudongmar Lake – Chopta Valley Excursion – Lachung
activities:
Wake up early, enjoy a good breakfast, check out of the hotel in Lachen and get ready for a day that is honestly hard to put into words.

Gurudongmar Lake

A three hour drive brings you up to a valley sitting at 11,800 feet, home to one of the highest lakes in the world. Gurudongmar Lake is considered sacred by Sikhs, Buddhists and Hindus alike, and the moment you set eyes on it, that sense of reverence feels completely natural. Snow covered peaks surround it through every season of the year, and the lake sits close to the Tibet border, adding a certain quiet intensity to the whole experience.

Cold Desert

This is where the Himalayan rain shadow zone blends into the Tibetan plateau, creating a landscape that feels unlike anything else. The mountains here rise to somewhere between 20,000 and 25,000 feet and are washed in the most striking and beautiful tones of colour.

Chopta Valley

Perched at 13,200 feet, Chopta Valley is a wonderfully scenic spot known for its ever changing shades and colours. The river here also draws adventure lovers who come every year to enjoy water sports against that stunning backdrop.

Thangu Valley

Thangu is a snug little village dressed up in bright alpine flowers that give it a very cheerful and welcoming feel. Hikers and nature lovers find themselves drawn here year after year for its gorgeous trails, and if you love photography, this place will keep your camera very busy.

The Lachung Monastery

After taking in all of this, continue the drive and arrive at Lachung where you will check in at the hotel and head out to visit the Lachung Monastery. This ancient Nyingma Buddhist gompa sits at 9,600 feet and carries centuries of history within its walls. It also hosts a famous mask dance each year that is truly something to witness if you happen to be around during that time. Settle in for a comfortable overnight stay in Lachung.

itinerary.title: Lachung – Yumthang Excursion – Gangtok
activities:
Today belongs to Yumthang Valley, more lovingly known as the Valley of Flowers, and it is every bit as magical as that name suggests. Start the morning with a satisfying breakfast, check out of the hotel and make your way up to 11,800 feet where this breathtaking valley waits to welcome you. While you are here, do not miss the famous hot spring that has earned quite a reputation over the years for its healing properties, particularly for skin. Spend as much time as you need soaking in the beauty of the valley before making your way toward Gangtok.

Singhik and Mangan

On the drive back, you will pass through Singhik and Mangan, two scenic little towns that offer their own quiet charm. If the sky decides to cooperate and stays clear, you are in for some truly stunning views of the Himalayan ranges, with possible glimpses of peaks like Kanchenjunga, Pandim, Simvo, Kabru, Jopuno and Mt. Siniolchu stretching out across the horizon.

Optional Tour to Zero Point / Additional Charges / Special Permit For those who want to push a little further, an optional visit to Zero Point can be arranged on request. Sitting at 15,300 feet, it marks the very last point where civilians are permitted to go, with the international border of China lying just a few meters beyond. It is a humbling and unforgettable spot to stand at. After wrapping up the day's sightseeing, continue the drive to Gangtok, check in at the hotel and ease into a cosy and restful overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) (130km / 4 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities: And just like that, the last day of your Sikkim holiday has quietly crept up on you. Sit down for one final breakfast, take a moment to soak in the surroundings one last time, and then wrap up the check out formalities. Your transfer to the railway station, bus station or airport will be all sorted out according to your travel plan, so there is nothing to worry about on that front. As you head back home with a bag full of memories and maybe a few extra kilos worth of souvenirs, we genuinely hope that every bit of this trip felt just right. It was a pleasure having you with us, and we truly hope to be a part of your next adventure whenever the travel bug bites again.

AllPackage.name: Shimla Manali Honeymoon Escape
AllPackage.description:
This six-day, five-night journey through Himachal Pradesh promises a chance to experience the charming hill stations of Shimla and Manali.

It's a chance to experience the mountains, explore local sights, and enjoy some well-deserved relaxation.

The journey begins in Shimla, a hill station that once served as a favored escape for the British Raj. It's known for its colonial architecture, pleasant weather, and breathtaking views.

Following that, the schedule calls for a trip to Kufri, a hill station renowned for its sweeping panoramas and inherent beauty. The plan also encompasses visits to Jakhoo Temple, perched on Shimla's tallest peak, and the bustling Mall Road, a hub of local commerce and cultural activity.

The drive from Shimla to Manali, a real treat, takes you through the breathtaking Kullu Valley. The drive along this route is a visual feast, showcasing river valleys, dense pine forests, and imposing mountains. It's a trip where the scenery is the star of the show.

In Manali, Solang Valley draws visitors with its expansive vistas and a host of adventure options. Paragliding, skiing (when the season's right), and the thrill of ropeway rides are all on offer. The valley itself is a blend of stunning scenery and opportunities for action.

The itinerary also includes a tour of Manali, highlighting some of its most well-known attractions. We'll visit the Hadimba Devi Temple, which is beautifully situated amidst cedar trees, and the Vashisht Temple, celebrated for its natural hot springs. Furthermore, we'll wander through the surrounding gardens and enjoy the vistas from several observation points.

The tour offers a well-rounded experience, blending scenic drives, breathtaking mountain vistas, cultural sites, and the chance for adventure, all within two of Himachal Pradesh's most popular destinations.
AllPackage.shortDescription: This 5N/6D tour covers Shimla & Manali, including Kufri, Solang Valley, temples, and scenic drives via Kullu Valley, blending mountain views, local sightseeing, and leisure experiences.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Misty mountain slope with lush green grass of Manali, scattered pine trees, rocky cliffs, and thin waterfalls beneath heavy gray clouds.

itinerary.title: Delhi to Shimla
activities:
Arrival and pickup from Delhi followed by transfer to Shimla by car. The journey passes through changing landscapes from plains to hills, offering views of winding roads, valleys, and pine forests.

On arrival in Shimla, check-in at the hotel in the evening. Rest of the day is at leisure. Overnight stay in Shimla.

itinerary.title: Shimla Sightseeing
activities:
After breakfast, proceed for a full-day sightseeing tour of Shimla. Visit Kufri, known for its scenic viewpoints and natural surroundings. Continue to Jakhoo Temple, located on the highest point of Shimla.

Later, explore The Ridge and Christ Church, followed by leisure time at Mall Road.

Return to hotel. Overnight stay in Shimla.

itinerary.title: Shimla to Manali via Kullu
activities:
After breakfast, check-out from hotel and proceed towards Manali via Kullu Valley.

Enroute, visit Pandoh Dam and enjoy views of the river and surrounding mountains. Optional river rafting can be experienced in Kullu.

On arrival in Manali, check-in at hotel and relax. Overnight stay in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali to Solang Valley
activities:
After breakfast, proceed for a day excursion to Solang Valley. The valley is known for its open landscapes and mountain views.

Travelers can enjoy optional adventure activities such as paragliding, ropeway rides, and skiing (seasonal). Spend time exploring the valley and enjoying the natural surroundings.

Return to hotel in Manali. Overnight stay in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali Sightseeing
activities:
After breakfast, proceed for local sightseeing in Manali. Visit Hadimba Devi Temple, surrounded by cedar forests. Continue to Manu Temple and Nehru Kund.

Also visit Manali Gompa and relax at Van Vihar.

Return to hotel. Overnight stay in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali to Delhi
activities: After breakfast, check-out from hotel and transfer back to Delhi. Drop at Airport or Railway Station for onward journey.

AllPackage.name: Pelling Gangtok Romance
AllPackage.description: Finding the right destinations to make your holiday truly special does not have to feel like a task. Our Gangtok Lachung Lachen Pelling holiday tour package takes care of all of that and then some. Beautifully crafted monasteries, lively marketplaces and mountain views that make your jaw drop are just a few of the many reasons people find themselves drawn to this wonderful northeastern state. The journey takes you through wide open semi-arid plains and over several motorable mountain passes that are an experience in themselves. Sikkim has a way of getting under your skin with its vibrant culture, one of a kind cuisine and scenic spots that look almost too good to be real. Reach out to our travel experts who will put together a deal that works around exactly what you are looking for. Our detailed itinerary covers every sightseeing spot worth visiting, so if you have been waiting for the right moment to explore these stunning foothills, booking our travel package is the best place to start.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Finding the right holiday destination does not have to be hard. Our Gangtok Lachung Lachen Pelling package brings together stunning monasteries, lively markets and breathtaking mountain views for a trip that gets under your skin and stays there.

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) – Gangtok (130 km / 4 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities: The moment you step off at Bagdogra Airport, the bus station or the railway station, one of our team members will be right there to welcome you and get things moving smoothly. As soon as you set foot on this lush and green part of the world, you will begin a four hour drive that takes you straight into the heart of Gangtok, a city that has grown into a vibrant hub of culture, art and some truly wonderful food. Check in at the hotel on arrival, freshen up and let yourself settle in at your own pace. The rest of the day is yours to enjoy however you like. When evening comes around, we would really encourage you to take a walk along MG Marg. It is lively, colourful and full of little shops where you can try out local food and pick up some beautiful art and handcrafted pieces to take home. Nepalese dresses, Tibetan carpets, alpine cheese, hand woven jackets, electronics and bamboo and cane baskets are some of the most popular things people love to bring back from here. Head back to the hotel when you are ready and enjoy a relaxed and comfortable overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok (Tsomgo Lake Excursion and Baba Mandir)
activities:
The second day opens with a good and nourishing breakfast at the hotel before heading out for a day of sightseeing that is going to be hard to forget. The first destination is Tsomgo Lake, also widely known as Changu Lake. A three hour drive takes you up to 12,400 feet where this stunning glacial lake sits in complete stillness. The locals hold it as a sacred place and the way the surrounding hills reflect off the surface of the water is the kind of thing that genuinely stops you in your tracks. A small temple sits quietly along the shore, adding to the peaceful and spiritual atmosphere of the place.

From there, the journey continues to Baba Harbhajan Mandir, perched at 13,200 feet with views that are nothing short of extraordinary. This shrine was built in memory of an Indian soldier who lost his life drowning in a nearby stream. His clothes, shoes, badges and photographs are all carefully preserved here, keeping his memory very much alive. It is considered mandatory for army officials to come and pay their respects, as it is widely believed that his soul continues to watch over and protect his fellow soldiers to this day. Many visitors also carry away bottled water from here, believing it holds healing properties for those who are unwell. If you are up for it, an optional tour to Nathula Pass can be arranged at an additional cost, where you can also enjoy a ride on beautifully decorated yaks and ponies. Head back to the hotel in Gangtok afterward for a restful overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – Lachen (125 Km / 6 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities:
Fill up with a good breakfast, check out of the hotel in Gangtok and get an early start to the day. The drive takes you through beautiful apple orchards and climbs up to a mesmerizing altitude of 8,800 feet as you make your way toward Lachung, a place that sits close to the Tibetan border and is home to the historic 19th century Buddhist Lachung Monastery. Along the way, there are a couple of stops that are absolutely worth your time.

Singhik View Point

The Singhik View Point feels like a world away from the noise and crowds of city life. It is a genuinely peaceful spot that rewards you with breathtaking views of Mt. Kanchenjunga and Mt. Siniolchu stretching out across the horizon, the kind of views that remind you why you travelled all this way.

Seven Sisters Waterfalls

The Seven Sisters Waterfall is one of the most beautiful and unspoiled waterfalls in the entire region. It gets its name from the way it tumbles down in seven distinct stages in a rhythm that is almost hypnotic to watch. Standing before it, you will find it very hard to look away.

Naga Waterfalls

The Naga Waterfalls bring a completely different kind of energy. A wide and powerful rush of water thunders down at tremendous speed, giving you a thrilling and immersive experience that is equally exciting and humbling. Stand too close and you will likely walk away soaking wet. After taking in all of these wonderful sights, continue the drive to Lachung. Check in at the hotel on arrival, sit down to a delicious dinner and enjoy a comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Lachen – Gurudongmar Lake – Chopta Valley Excursion – Lachung
activities:
Wake up early, enjoy a good breakfast, check out of the hotel in Lachen and get ready for a day that covers some genuinely remarkable ground.

Gurudongmar Lake

The drive to Gurudongmar Lake takes about three hours and brings you up to a peak sitting at 17,000 feet, placing it among the highest lakes in all of India. The lake sits very close to the Tibet border and is surrounded by snow covered peaks throughout the entire year. Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists all consider it sacred, and the serene stillness of the place makes that feel completely natural the moment you arrive.

Chopta Valley

Chopta Valley is a strikingly beautiful destination that sits at 13,200 feet and is loved for the way its colours shift and change across the landscape. Adventure lovers are particularly drawn here for the hiking trails and the water sports activities that the valley has to offer.

Thangu Valley

Thangu is a snug little village dressed in bright alpine flowers that give it a cheerful and welcoming character. It draws a steady stream of travellers every year who come specifically for the wonderful hiking trails that wind through the valley.

After these stops, check out of the hotel post lunch and continue the journey toward Lachung. On arrival, check in and head straight out to visit the Lachung Monastery, an ancient Nyingma Buddhist gompa sitting at an impressive 9,600 feet. If your visit happens to fall around the festive season, the famous mask dance held here each year is something you absolutely should not miss. Settle in for a comfortable overnight stay in Lachung.

itinerary.title: Lachung – Yumthang Excursion – Gangtok
activities:
Today takes you to Yumthang Valley, lovingly called the Valley of Flowers, and it is one of those places that genuinely lives up to everything said about it. Start the morning with a good breakfast, check out of the hotel and make your way up to 11,800 feet where this stunning valley opens up around you. If you have the time, do stop by the famous hot spring along the way, which has built quite a reputation for its healing properties for various skin conditions.

Bheema and Twin Falls

On the drive back toward Gangtok, you will pass by two beautiful cascades, Bheema Falls and Twin Falls. Both leave a lasting impression and are the kind of sights that make you want to pull over and just stand there for a while. If the weather is kind and the skies stay clear, you will also be treated to sweeping views of the eastern Himalayan ranges that are hard to put into words.

Optional Tour to Zero Point / Additional Charges / Special Permit For those who want to push a little further, an optional visit to Zero Point can be arranged on request. Sitting at 15,300 feet, it marks the last point where civilians are permitted to go, with the international border of China lying just a few meters beyond. It is a place that carries a weight and significance you feel deeply the moment you are standing there. After wrapping up the sightseeing, continue the drive to Gangtok, check in at the hotel and ease into a warm and cosy overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – Pelling (120 km / 5.5 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities: Wake up to a warm and satisfying breakfast, soak in the last few moments of Gangtok and then check out of the hotel as you get ready to move on. The drive to Pelling is one that has a character all of its own, taking you through landscapes that feel deeply alive with history, mystic rituals and the kind of cultural richness that you sense even through the car window. It is a land that carries its traditions close and wears them with quiet pride. On arriving in Pelling, check in at the hotel and let the rest of the day unfold at whatever pace feels right. Enjoy a relaxed and comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Full Day Local Sightseeing in Pelling
activities:
Get an early start with a delicious breakfast and step out for a day that takes you through the very best of what Pelling has to offer.

Darap Valley

The first stop is Darap Valley, a charming little hamlet that is perfect for slowing right down. The locals here are genuinely warm and welcoming, and spending time with them gives you a lovely and honest window into everyday Sikkimese life. It is the kind of place that reminds you that travel is as much about people as it is about scenery.

Rimbi Waterfalls and Kanchenjunga Waterfalls

Next up are the Rimbi and Kanchenjunga Waterfalls, two perennial cascades that have a wonderfully refreshing effect on the mind, body and spirit. Beyond just being beautiful to look at, they are also popular spots for fishing and other recreational activities.

Rock Garden and Khecheopalri Lake

The Rock Garden is a lovely place to wander through, with gardens, pools and a small stream running through it and winding footpaths that invite you to take your time. The Khecheopalri Lake nearby is one of the most sacred water bodies in Pelling and what makes it particularly fascinating is that despite sitting deep within a thick forest, its surface stays completely free of floating leaves, adding to its almost otherworldly sense of calm.

Rabdentse Ruins, Pema Yangtse Monastery and Helipad Ground The Rabdentse Ruins are a deeply compelling stop for anyone with even a passing interest in history or archaeology, telling the story of Sikkim's rich and layered past through every worn stone and crumbling wall. A short walk from there brings you to Pema Yangtse Monastery, where the views of the Kanchenjunga ranges are breathtaking. The Helipad Ground rounds off the day perfectly as a stunning viewpoint for the snow capped peaks, and the sunset witnessed from here is the kind that leaves everyone standing in silence. Head back to the hotel in the evening for a well earned overnight stay in Pelling.

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) (160 km / 6 Hours Drive Approximately)
activities: All good things take their time to end, and today marks the final morning of your Sikkim holiday. Sit down for one last breakfast, take a quiet moment to look back at everything this trip brought your way, and then wrap up the check out formalities. Your transfer to the railway station, bus station or airport will be arranged according to your travel plan, so the journey home is taken care of without any fuss. You are leaving with a heart full of memories, a bag full of souvenirs and hopefully a smile that stays for a long time. It has been a genuine pleasure being part of your travels, and we truly hope that when the next adventure calls, you think of us again.

AllPackage.name: Kerala Honeymoon Paradise
AllPackage.description: Kerala has a gentleness to it that very few places in the world can match, and this 5 Nights 6 Days tour lets you experience the very best of it. From the cool mist covered hills of Munnar and the rich aroma of tea and spice plantations to the wild and unhurried beauty of Thekkady where the forest meets the water at Periyar Lake, every day brings a completely different side of this incredible state. Then comes Alleppey, where you trade the hills for the backwaters and spend a night drifting along on a traditional houseboat, surrounded by swaying palms, still green waters and a silence that feels like a proper exhale. Cochin ties it all together with its own distinct blend of history, culture and coastal charm. This trip is not just a tour, it is Kerala at its most complete, nature, wildlife, waterways and warm local life all woven into one beautifully balanced journey.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Kerala slows you down in the best way. This 5 Nights 6 Days tour takes you through Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey and Cochin, covering misty hills, spice plantations, wildlife, backwaters and a houseboat stay that you will never forget.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Boat gliding on calm river in Munnar, Kerala, with lush forest reflections and a herd of elephants walking along the riverbank.

itinerary.title: Cochin to Munnar
activities: Arrival at Cochin Airport or Railway Station followed by transfer to Munnar. Enjoy scenic views including forests, waterfalls, and plantations during the journey. Check-in at hotel and rest. Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar Sightseeing
activities:
After breakfast, proceed for a full-day sightseeing tour of Munnar. Visit tea plantations, viewpoints, and nearby attractions. Explore the natural beauty of the region with its rolling hills, cool climate, and lush greenery.

Return to the hotel for overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar to Thekkady
activities:
After breakfast, check-out and transfer to Thekkady. Upon arrival, visit a spice plantation to understand the cultivation of cardamom, pepper, cinnamon, coffee, and tea.

Later, enjoy boating at Periyar Lake, located within Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary. The area is known for its natural surroundings and possible wildlife sightings.

Overnight stay in Thekkady.

itinerary.title: Thekkady to Alleppey – Houseboat Stay
activities:
After breakfast, transfer to Alleppey. On arrival, check-in to a traditional Kerala houseboat.

Enjoy a backwater cruise through interconnected canals, lagoons, and village areas. Observe daily life along the waterways, paddy fields, and coconut groves. Meals are served onboard during the cruise.

Overnight stay in houseboat.

itinerary.title: Alleppey to Cochin
activities:
After breakfast, check-out from the houseboat and transfer to Cochin.

On arrival, check-in at the hotel. The rest of the day is free for leisure or optional local exploration. Overnight stay in Cochin.

itinerary.title: Departure
activities: After breakfast, transfer to Cochin Airport or Railway Station for departure, marking the end of the tour.

AllPackage.name: Kashmir Honeymoon Dreams
AllPackage.description: Kashmir is one of those places that gets into your heart and simply refuses to leave. This 4 Nights 5 Days tour takes you through the very best of it, covering Srinagar, Gulmarg and Pahalgam in a journey that feels equal parts relaxing and deeply memorable. You will spend a night on a traditional houseboat on the legendary Dal Lake and glide across its calm waters on a shikara as the mountains reflect on the surface around you. The sightseeing in Srinagar walks you through the grand Mughal Gardens and up to the hilltop Shankaracharya Temple where the views of the valley will stop you in your tracks. A day in Gulmarg introduces you to meadows, mountain air and an optional gondola ride that takes you higher than most experiences ever will. Pahalgam then brings you face to face with the Lidder River and a valley so beautiful it feels almost unreal. This trip is nature, culture, history and soul all rolled into one, and Kashmir delivers every single bit of it.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Kashmir does not just impress you, it stays with you. This 4 Nights 5 Days tour takes you through Srinagar, Gulmarg and Pahalgam, covering houseboat stays, shikara rides, Mughal Gardens, mountain meadows and the beautiful Lidder River.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Gondola ride over snowy mountains in Kashmir, with pine forests, skiers on slopes, and clear blue sky in a scenic winter landscape.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Jammu – Transfer to Srinagar – Houseboat Stay
activities: Your Kashmir adventure begins the moment you step off at Jammu Railway Station, where our representative will be waiting to welcome you and take care of everything from here. Settle into the vehicle and let the journey to Srinagar unfold around you. The drive itself is a preview of the beauty that lies ahead, with landscapes that gradually shift and open up into something truly breathtaking as you climb higher. Once you arrive in Srinagar, you will not be checking into just any hotel. Tonight, your home is a traditional houseboat on the legendary Dal Lake, one of those experiences that people dream about for years before actually living it. Get settled in, breathe in the fresh Kashmir air and then step into a shikara for a one hour ride across the lake. The water is calm, the mountains are reflected on the surface and the whole world feels wonderfully far away. As the evening light settles over Dal Lake and the houseboat lamps flicker on around you, you will know without any doubt that this trip is going to be something special. Enjoy a warm dinner on the houseboat and drift off to sleep to the gentle sound of water all around you.

itinerary.title: Srinagar Local Sightseeing
activities: Wake up to the sight of Dal Lake right outside your window, one of those morning views that no alarm clock can ruin. After a good breakfast, head out to explore the garden city of Srinagar, a place that has inspired poets and painters for centuries and will very likely inspire you too. The Mughal Gardens are your first stop and they are every bit as grand and beautiful as their name suggests. Begin at Cheshma Shahi, the smallest yet most charming of the three, fed by a natural spring that the Mughals believed had medicinal properties. From there, move on to Shalimar Garden, built by Emperor Jahangir as a gift of love for his queen Noor Jahan, a place where terraced lawns, marble pavilions and cascading water channels come together in perfect harmony. Nishat Garden rounds off the trio with its dramatic twelve terraced levels climbing up toward the Zabarwan Mountains and overlooking Dal Lake below. Each garden has its own personality and together they give you a real sense of the elegance and vision that defined the Mughal era. Later in the day, make your way up to Shankaracharya Temple, perched on a hilltop at 1,000 feet above the valley floor. The climb is worth every step for the panoramic views of Srinagar, the surrounding mountains and the shimmering Dal Lake that await you at the top. Head back to the hotel in the evening, check in and rest up after a day that has given you so much to take in.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Gulmarg – Return to Srinagar
activities: After breakfast, hit the road toward Gulmarg, a name that literally translates to Meadow of Flowers and lives up to every bit of that description. The drive takes you through some wonderfully scenic stretches of Kashmir countryside that make the journey just as enjoyable as the destination. Gulmarg sits at around 2,650 meters and on a clear day the views of the surrounding peaks are the kind that make you forget what you were thinking about. Wander through the open meadows, take in the famous golf course that is one of the highest in the world and soak in a landscape that shifts from lush green in summer to a pristine white wonderland in winter. The highlight for many visitors is the Gondola ride, one of the highest cable car rides in Asia, which lifts you up through two phases to a viewpoint that offers a perspective of the Himalayas that simply cannot be described in words, only felt. If you are feeling adventurous, a short trek through the surrounding terrain is another way to get even closer to the raw beauty of this place. Head back to Srinagar in the evening with a full heart and enjoy a comfortable overnight stay at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Pahalgam – Return to Srinagar
activities: Today takes you to Pahalgam, widely known as the Valley of Shepherds, and the drive there is as much a part of the experience as the destination itself. The route passes through Pampore, famous for its vast saffron fields that turn a stunning purple during blooming season. You will then roll through Avantipura, where ancient temple ruins tell quiet stories of a civilisation that flourished here centuries ago, before continuing through Bijbehara and Anantnag, each with their own distinct character and charm. Pahalgam itself is a place of extraordinary natural beauty, cradled by pine forests, snow capped peaks and the sound of the Lidder River rushing through the valley. Walk along the riverbank and let the cool mountain air and the sound of the water do what no spa ever quite manages. The scenery here is the kind that feels almost too perfect, the sort of landscape you half expect to see on a painting rather than right in front of you. Spend as much time here as the day allows before making your way back to Srinagar for the final overnight stay at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Departure
activities: The last morning in Kashmir arrives quietly and with it comes that bittersweet feeling of a trip well lived. Sit down for one final breakfast and let the memories of the past few days settle warmly around you. Dal Lake at dawn, the grandeur of the Mughal Gardens, the mountain views from Gulmarg, the Lidder River at Pahalgam. Each one a moment worth carrying home. When you are ready, your transfer to Jammu Railway Station will be arranged smoothly and you will begin the journey back with a heart that is genuinely fuller than when you arrived. Kashmir has a way of doing that to people, and we have a feeling this will not be your last time here.

AllPackage.name: Kerala Honeymoon Bliss
AllPackage.description:
This 5 Nights 6 Days Kerala tour covers key destinations including Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, and Kovalam, offering a well-balanced mix of hill stations, wildlife, backwaters, and coastal experiences.

The adventure starts in Munnar, a hill station celebrated for its undulating tea estates, shrouded valleys, and agreeable weather. Visitors can soak in the area's natural splendor, with its picturesque vistas, serpentine roads, cascading waterfalls, and sweeping viewpoints.

Next, the journey takes us to Thekkady, where the celebrated Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary is located. Guests can wander through spice plantations, where cardamom, pepper, cinnamon, and coffee are grown. A boat ride on Periyar Lake offers a chance to see the forest and, occasionally, catch a glimpse of wildlife near the water's edge.

Next, we'll head to Alleppey, a place celebrated for its complex network of backwaters.

Spending time on a classic houseboat offers a unique experience. It's an opportunity to slowly navigate tranquil canals, lagoons, and the scenery of nearby villages.

The backwaters present a window into a landscape of rice paddies, gently bending coconut palms, and the daily rhythms that play out along the water's edge. It's a peaceful, captivating experience.

The final destination is Kovalam, a coastal paradise known for its sun-drenched beaches and relaxed atmosphere.

Visitors can take their time near the water, enjoying the salty breeze and the laid-back vibe that comes with being by the sea. It's a world away from the hills and quiet spots they'd just experienced.

The planned trip paints a vivid picture of Kerala's diverse scenery. It includes everything from the breathtaking views of hill stations and visits to tea plantations to wildlife spotting, serene backwater cruises, and relaxing days at the beach. This itinerary is designed to give you a comprehensive experience of the area.
AllPackage.shortDescription: This 5N/6D Kerala tour covers Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey & Kovalam, featuring hill views, wildlife, backwaters with houseboat stay, and beach relaxation in one journey.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Winding road through lush green tea plantations in Munnar, Kerala, with misty hills and golden sunrise over rolling valleys.

itinerary.title: Cochin to Munnar
activities: Your Kerala journey begins the moment you step off at Cochin Airport or Railway Station, where our representative will be waiting to welcome you and take care of your transfer to Munnar. The drive to Munnar is an experience in itself, winding through dense forests, past cascading waterfalls and alongside fragrant spice and tea plantations that give you your very first taste of Kerala's extraordinary natural beauty. As the hills grow greener and the air turns cooler and fresher, you will feel the pace of everyday life slowly begin to ease. Arrive at the hotel, check in and give yourself the rest of the day to simply breathe, settle in and prepare for the wonderful days ahead. Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar Sightseeing
activities: Wake up to cool mountain air and the sight of mist rolling gently over the tea covered hills outside your window. After a good breakfast, head out to explore the very best of Munnar. The endless stretches of tea plantations that blanket every hillside in every direction are a sight that genuinely takes your breath away, and no camera ever quite does them justice. Visit the Tea Museum to understand the fascinating journey of a tea leaf from bush to cup. Eravikulam National Park is home to the rare and charming Nilgiri Tahr and offers some of the most stunning high altitude landscape in all of Kerala. Mattupetty Dam and its surrounding lake provide a peaceful spot for boating against a backdrop of forested hills. Attukal Waterfalls and Top Station, the highest viewpoint in Munnar with sweeping views stretching across into Tamil Nadu, round off a day that feels like a slow and beautiful immersion into one of India's finest hill stations. Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar to Thekkady
activities: After breakfast, check out and make your way toward Thekkady, where Kerala gets wonderfully wild. The drive through the hills and forests sets the tone perfectly for what this destination is all about. Upon arrival, head straight into a spice plantation tour that is one of the most sensory rich experiences this trip has to offer. Walk through estates growing cardamom, cinnamon, pepper, coffee and tea, with guides explaining how each plant grows, how it is harvested and what makes Kerala spices so sought after across the world. The air is thick with fragrance and every turn reveals something new and fascinating. In the afternoon, make your way to Periyar Lake for a boat ride through the heart of the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary. The lake is calm and the forest presses right up to its edges. Elephants, bison, deer and a rich variety of birds come to the banks, and simply drifting quietly through this landscape with the one you love is an experience that sits with you long after the trip is over. Overnight stay in Thekkady.

itinerary.title: Thekkady to Alleppey – Houseboat Stay
activities: After breakfast, check out of the hotel and begin the journey toward Alleppey, the backwater capital of Kerala and one of the most romantically unique destinations in the entire country. On arrival, step aboard your private traditional houseboat, a beautifully appointed kettuvallam that will be your floating home for the night. As the houseboat moves slowly through a network of tranquil canals, lagoons and waterways, the world outside becomes a series of postcard perfect scenes. Coconut palms lean over the water, paddy fields stretch out in vivid green, and village life plays out gently along the banks as if time has slowed down entirely just for you. Sit out on the deck together and watch it all drift past. As the evening arrives, the houseboat comes alive with a specially arranged candle light dinner set against the most romantic backdrop imaginable, still water, soft light and complete quiet all around you. Your cabin has been beautifully decorated just for the occasion. Fall asleep to the gentle sound of the water and the rustle of the palms, and wake up to a morning on the backwaters that you will never forget. Overnight stay on houseboat.

itinerary.title: Alleppey to Kovalam
activities: After a leisurely breakfast on the houseboat, check out and make your way to Kovalam, where Kerala trades its waterways for the open sea. The drive south through the coastal landscape of Kerala builds a quiet anticipation as the Arabian Sea gradually comes into view. Kovalam is home to one of the most beautiful crescent shaped beaches in India, and the moment you step onto that golden sand with the sound of the waves in front of you and the sway of the coconut palms behind, everything feels effortlessly right. Spend the evening walking along the shore, watching the famous Kovalam lighthouse catch the last light of the day and letting the sea breeze do what it does best. Overnight stay in Kovalam.

itinerary.title: Departure
activities: The final morning arrives quietly, as last mornings of good trips always do. Sit down for one last breakfast and let the memories of everything this journey brought you wash over you warmly. Munnar's misty hills, the wild beauty of Thekkady, a night floating on the backwaters of Alleppey and the sound of the sea at Kovalam. Each one a memory worth holding onto. When you are ready, your transfer to Trivandrum Airport or Railway Station will be arranged smoothly and your journey home begins. Kerala has a way of staying with people long after they leave, and we have a feeling you will be back.

AllPackage.name: Gangtok to Pelling – Your Perfect Sikkim Honeymoon
AllPackage.description: Two people coming together in marriage is the start of something truly lifelong. It is a relationship woven with love, trust, deep honesty and the kind of romance that needs to be nurtured and celebrated. A honeymoon is that beautiful window right after the wedding where all of that comes naturally. Away from the noise and the relatives and the rituals, it is just the two of you building memories that will make you smile decades later. Picking the right destination for this trip is everything, and nothing sets the mood quite like waking up to misty mountain valleys and crisp fresh air. We have done the thinking for you and put together something we are genuinely proud of. Sikkim sits quietly in the northeastern corner of India and has a rare kind of beauty that does not need to announce itself. It simply shows up and takes your breath away. Our Spectacular Sikkim Honeymoon Package is designed to walk you through two places that capture the very soul of this state, the vibrant and warm capital city of Gangtok and the peaceful, increasingly beloved hill town of Pelling.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Sikkim's misty valleys, peaceful lakes and ancient monasteries make it the perfect honeymoon setting. Our Gangtok and Pelling package is designed to give your new beginning the backdrop it truly deserves.
AllPackage.imageAlt: Hiker climbing over a rock in a snowy mountain valley in Sikkim, surrounded by towering snow-covered Himalayan peaks under a bright blue sky.

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) – Gangtok (130 km / 4 hrs drive)
activities: Step off at Bagdogra Airport or NJP Railway Station and our representative will be right there to greet you and take care of your transfer to the hotel in Gangtok. This city has a beauty that is genuinely hard to put into words. Surrounded by majestic mountain ranges, a culture that pulls you in and food that keeps you coming back for more, Gangtok has a way of leaving every visitor completely charmed. Check in at the hotel, rest up and let yourself settle in. When the evening rolls around, head out for a leisurely walk along MG Marg with your beloved. Stroll through the streets, take in the atmosphere and let the night sky above Gangtok set the mood for the beautiful days ahead. Head back to your room when you are ready and get a good night of sleep.

itinerary.title: Gangtok (Full day local sightseeing)
activities:
Fuel up with a good breakfast and get ready for a day packed with some of the finest sights Gangtok has to offer. Begin at Bakthang Waterfalls, where crystal clear water rushes down through lush green creepers in a way that is genuinely worth stopping for. Close by is Tashi View Point, a wonderfully clean and open spot famous for its stunning views of Mt. Kanchenjunga and Mt. Siniolchu and a favourite among both locals and visitors. From there, head to Ganesh Tok, a shrine dedicated to Lord Ganesha that doubles up as a lovely viewpoint overlooking nearby mountain ranges and rivers, a spot that feels both spiritually grounding and visually rewarding.

Next on the list is Enchey Monastery, a 200 year old structure that still stands with quiet dignity and is said to have received the blessings of the saint Lama Dhrupthob Karpo. After that, make your way to the Directorate of Handicraft and Handloom, a paradise for anyone who appreciates traditional art. Pick up some authentic woven blankets, wooden showpieces or shawls to carry a little piece of Sikkim back home.

Grab lunch at a restaurant that catches your eye and then continue to Do Drul Chorten Stupa, a sacred structure built in 1945 featuring 108 prayer wheels. Wrap up the afternoon with a visit to the Institute of Tibetology, home to a remarkable collection of Tibetan cultural artefacts, followed by the Flower Exhibition Center and finally the Ropeway and Banjhakri Falls, a beautiful waterfall spread across two acres. It has been quite a day, so head back to the hotel, rest your feet and drift off into a well deserved sleep.

itinerary.title: Gangtok (Tsomgo Lake Excursion)
activities:
Set off for the day with Tsomgo Lake as your destination, a sacred and strikingly beautiful lake sitting at 12,400 feet above sea level. The locals hold it in deep reverence, and once you are standing at its edge, that feeling makes complete sense. Bring your camera because this place is endlessly photogenic. The lake shifts colours with the seasons, turning a vivid aquamarine in summer, freezing into a glittering white in winter and bursting into a riot of reflected colours during spring when the flowers bloom around it. No matter when you visit, it never disappoints.

Nearby is Baba Harbhajan Mandir, a memorial dedicated to late Sepoy Harbhajan Singh who gave his life to save a group of mules. It is widely believed that his soul continues to watch over the soldiers stationed in the surrounding areas and warns them of approaching danger. Visit this extraordinary place and take a moment to honour the spirit of a true brave heart. Head back to the hotel in the evening, unwind at your own pace and spend the night in comfort.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – Pelling (120 km / 5.5 hrs drive) via Namchi and Ravangla
activities:
After breakfast, set off toward Pelling, a peaceful town tucked away within dense forests, far from the noise of everyday life and just the kind of place you want to be with your partner. It is steadily growing into one of Sikkim's most loved destinations, giving Gangtok a good run for its title. On the way, stop at the Namchi Char Dham Temple, a beautiful religious and cultural centre dedicated to Lord Shiva, and the Samdruptse Statue, an elegant depiction of Guru Padmasambhava set upon a hill believed to grant wishes. Both are absolutely worth your time.

Take a short diversion to Ravangla, a charming little tourist town in South Sikkim sitting at 8,000 feet. It is relatively newly discovered on the tourist trail but already turning heads with its scenic beauty. Here you will visit the Buddha Park, where a magnificent statue of Maitreya Buddha stands against a backdrop of towering mountains, and the Temi Tea Gardens, a refreshing and visually stunning stretch of greenery that ranks among the finest tea gardens in the country. After soaking it all in, continue the drive to Pelling, check in at the hotel and spend the evening at your own pace before calling it a night.

itinerary.title: Pelling (Full day local sightseeing)
activities:
The fifth day is all about Pelling and everything this wonderful place has tucked away within it. Start with a good breakfast and then head out to see it all. First up is Darap Valley, a small and deeply peaceful village that feels tailor made for couples who just want to breathe and be together. From there, visit the Rimbi Falls nearby, a charming little waterfall that feeds the Rimbi River and is well loved for fishing and swimming. The Rock Garden comes next, a lovely spot shaded by rocks with benches along the riverside where you can simply sit and let the beauty of the surroundings sink in. After that, make your way to Kanchenjunga Waterfalls. The trek to reach them takes a little effort but the moment you see the water tearing through the rock cuts, every bit of that effort disappears instantly. Before breaking for lunch, visit the Khecheopalri Sacred Lake, a deeply revered pilgrimage site for both Buddhists and Hindus that is also widely believed to hold wish fulfilling powers.

Enjoy a satisfying lunch and then continue to the Rabdentse Ruins, a sobering and historically rich site that tells the story of the Gurkha army's invasion and the fall of Sikkim's former capital. Next is Pema Yangtse Monastery, one of the oldest monasteries in Sikkim dating back to 1705 and home to around 108 monks, a place that carries centuries of quiet devotion within its walls. Round off the day at the Helipad Ground, where the views of the surrounding mountain ranges are truly iconic. It has been a full and beautiful day, so head back to the hotel, lie down and let the memories of this last honeymoon night with your partner settle warmly around you.

itinerary.title: Pelling – New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) (160 km / 6 hrs drive)
activities: Check out of the hotel and begin the journey back to NJP or Bagdogra Airport, carrying with you a heart full of warm and beautiful memories. We hope this honeymoon gave you everything you were looking for and then a little more. Here is to this wonderful new chapter of your life together.

AllPackage.name: Gangtok Pelling Darjeeling – A Sikkim Love Story
AllPackage.description:
The wedding date is looming, and everything feels like a sprint. With the final touches and the general chaos, carving out a second to consider the honeymoon can feel like a Herculean task.

The seven sisters have long been considered one of the most breathtaking combinations this country has to offer for couples starting a new life together. Sikkim, one among these seven, carries a beauty that is entirely its own and nearly impossible to put into words. Darjeeling is small but it punches well above its weight when it comes to creating memories for couples who are just beginning their story together. Together, Gangtok, Pelling and Darjeeling make for a honeymoon trio that pulls you away from the rush of city life and wraps you in something far more beautiful. Read through the itinerary below to get a feel of everything waiting for you on this wonderful journey.
AllPackage.shortDescription: Sikkim and Darjeeling together make for a honeymoon that feels like a dream. From the romantic valleys of Gangtok and Pelling to the iconic toy trains of Darjeeling, our Romance in Sikkim package gives your new beginning the perfect setting.

Costs due to landslides, road blocks, or political disturbances (payable on the spot).

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) – Gangtok (130 km / 4 hrs drive)
activities: Your honeymoon begins the moment you step off at NJP or Bagdogra Airport, where our representative will be waiting to take care of your transfer to the hotel in Gangtok. The four to five hour drive up is a beautiful experience in itself, with Sikkim's stunning rhododendrons lining the way and your partner right beside you. It is the kind of drive that sets the mood perfectly for everything ahead. Stop for a few pictures along the route, check in at the hotel when you arrive and take some time to settle in and freshen up. Once you are feeling rested, head out for an evening walk along MG Road, stroll through the streets of Gangtok hand in hand and soak up the atmosphere. Head back to the room when the night draws in and get a good sleep before the adventures of the next day begin.

itinerary.title: Gangtok (Tsomgo Lake Excursion and Baba Mandir)
activities:
Start the day fresh with breakfast and set off for Tsomgo Lake by 8 in the morning. The two to three hour drive brings you up to 3,750 meters where this sacred and strikingly beautiful lake waits. In summer the water bursts into a collision of colours that is genuinely breathtaking, while winter transforms it into a frozen, sparkling white landscape. The rugged terrain and the towering mountains framing the lake make it one of the most naturally romantic backdrops you will find anywhere. Get your camera out and make the most of it. Just beside the lake is Baba Harbhajan Mandir, a shrine built in memory of 22 year old Sepoy Baba Harbhajan Singh, a young soldier whose story continues to move everyone who visits. The water here is believed to carry healing properties and locals hold firmly to the belief that his soul still watches over and protects the army personnel stationed nearby.

Head back to the hotel by evening and let the rest of the night be yours to enjoy. Take a walk around if you feel like it or simply sit down to a warm and satisfying dinner together. There is also an optional Nathu La Pass tour available at an additional cost, which can be arranged after the Baba Mandir visit. Once an ancient silk route between India and China, it offers extraordinary views of Tibet and the surrounding mountain ranges that are well worth the extra effort.

itinerary.title: Gangtok – Pelling (120 km / 5.5 hrs drive) via Namchi Char Dham and Samdruptse Statue
activities:
After breakfast, pack up and head toward Pelling, a quiet and charming little town that sits far from the rush of city life and is quickly becoming one of Sikkim's most talked about destinations after Gangtok. The views of Khangchendzonga and the surrounding ranges from here are the kind that stay with you. On the way, stop at the Namchi Char Dham Temple, a beautiful place of worship and cultural significance dedicated to Lord Shiva. Nearby stands the Samdruptse Statue on Samdruptse Hill, also known as the wish fulfilling hill. Local belief holds that the hill is a dormant volcano and that prayers are what keep it at rest. The towering statue of Guru Padmasambhava, a triumph of engineering that took seven years to complete, stands as a powerful symbol of peace and strength.

Continue the drive to Pelling after the sightseeing, check in at the hotel and let the evening be entirely yours. Sit out under the stars, wander around the hotel grounds, talk without any clock watching and simply enjoy being together in this beautiful place.

itinerary.title: Pelling (Full day local sightseeing)
activities:
Get ready for a day that keeps giving from start to finish. After breakfast, head out to explore Pelling at its very best. The first stop is Darap Valley, a small hamlet with a beauty that is hard to match and a young local community that is warm, aware and genuinely welcoming. Next is Rimbi Falls, close to Darap Valley and widely regarded as one of Pelling's finest attractions. The waters here create a lovely recreational spot for swimming and fishing that both locals and visitors enjoy thoroughly. Sewaro Rock Garden follows, offering stunning views of the skies above along with cafeterias and swimming pools that make it a great place to linger. From there, visit the Kanchenjunga Waterfalls, a perennial and incredibly popular spot, followed by the sacred Khecheopalri Lake, a pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Buddhists that carries a rare sense of calm. Keep clicking pictures through all of this because these are the memories you will come back to for years.

Head back to the hotel for lunch and a short rest before heading out again. The afternoon takes you to the Rabdentse Ruins, what remains of Sikkim's former capital after the Nepalese invasion in the 18th century, a deeply historical and quietly moving site. After that, visit Pema Yangtse Monastery, one of the oldest and most respected monasteries in Sikkim, dating back to 1705 and carrying a spiritual peace that is immediately felt. Round off the day at the Helipad Ground where the views of Pelling, Kangchenjunga and the surrounding ranges are simply stunning. Head back to the hotel after a full and wonderful day, have dinner and get a solid rest because tomorrow the journey moves on to Darjeeling.

itinerary.title: Pelling – Darjeeling
activities: Day five is a travel day and a welcome chance to simply be with each other. Have breakfast, double check your bags and set off for Darjeeling, roughly 73 kilometres from Pelling and about three to four hours away. Use the drive well. Talk, laugh, look out at the passing hills together and enjoy the kind of unhurried time that everyday life rarely allows. You will be at the hotel before you know it. Check in, pour yourself a cup of tea or coffee, sit back and let the charm of Darjeeling begin to settle around you. Enjoy a comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Darjeeling (Full day local sightseeing)
activities:
The alarm goes off early today and it is absolutely worth it. Leave for Tiger Hill at 4 in the morning and watch the sun rise over the Kanchenjunga ranges in one of the most spectacular displays of colour you will ever witness. Sharing that moment with the person you love makes it all the more special. Do not leave without capturing it. On the way back, stop at Ghoom Monastery, home to a magnificent 15 feet statue of Lord Buddha, and the Batasia Loop, a beautiful spiral train track surrounded by gardens and eateries that is a joy to walk around.

Return to the hotel for breakfast and then head out again for more. The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, established in 1954 to bring dignity and recognition to the sport of mountain climbing, is a fascinating visit. The Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park, closed on Thursdays, is home to the rare red panda and snow leopard among many other species. Continue to Tenzing Rock, where amateur and professional climbers each have their own side to explore, then Chitrey Tea Garden where fresh tea is brewed right from the plants growing in the backyard. End the day at the Japanese Temple and the Peace Pagoda, two structures that stand close together and are often visited as one. Built under the guidance of Japanese monk Nichidatsu Fujii, both carry a deep and grounding sense of peace and history.

Head back to the hotel when the day winds down, relax for a while and if the mood strikes, take a stroll down Mall Road or Chowrasta. Enjoy a delicious dinner and let this wonderful day end on a warm and contented note.

itinerary.title: Darjeeling – New Jalpaiguri Railway Station (NJP) / Bagdogra Airport (IXB) (88 km / 3 hrs drive)
activities: Pack up your bags along with every beautiful memory from these seven days and check out of the hotel for the last time. The drive to NJP Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport will likely bring back flashes of everything you experienced together on this trip. Let them come and hold onto every one of them. This honeymoon was just the beginning of a lifetime of adventures together, and we genuinely wish that your marriage only grows richer, deeper and more beautiful with every passing year.

AllPackage.description: The Hampta Pass Trek is one of the most scenic and adventurous treks in Himachal Pradesh, offering a perfect blend of lush green valleys, snow-covered mountains, rivers, waterfalls, and barren landscapes. Situated at an altitude of around 14,000 feet, the trek connects the beautiful Kullu Valley with the dramatic terrain of Spiti Valley. Ideal for both beginners and experienced trekkers, Hampta Pass is known for its changing landscapes and breathtaking Himalayan views. The trek usually takes 4 to 5 days and provides an unforgettable experience for nature lovers and adventure seekers looking to explore the beauty of the Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Manali to Chika Via Jobra
activities: The Hampta Pass trek begins with a beautiful 1-hour drive from Manali (6,700 ft) to Jobra (9,800 ft). It offers beautiful views of mountains around it .When you reach Jobra, the 2 km trek starts with a dense forest filled with pine, maple, and deodar trees. The path is easy to walk, which makes it a good start for the coming days. After walking for 2 hours, you will reach a place called Chika. It is high up in the mountains. The camp is in a big green area near a small and beautiful stream called Rani Nallah. It's a perfect place to rest, breathe in the fresh mountain air, and sleep under the stars on your first night.

itinerary.title: Chika Via Jobra to Balu ka Ghera
activities: The trek from Chika (10,100 ft) to Balu Ka Ghera (11,900 ft), covering a distance of 5 km in about 5 to 6 hours. The row is very beautiful and full of nature. In the route you can see green meadows, bright and colorful wildflowers. You can cross a small river along the route. You will walk beside a small stream called Rani Nallah. Big mountains can be seen all around. It looks very nice and calm. The route slowly climbs up but it is not too difficult. By evening, you will reach Balu Ka Ghera. It is a flat place at the bottom of Hampta Pass. You will set up your camp here for the night and see beautiful views of the Dhauladhar mountains.

itinerary.title: Balu ka Ghera to Shea goru
activities: The trek starts from Balu Ka Ghera (11,900 ft) and crosses the Hampta Pass (14,100 ft) to reach Shea goru (12,900 ft). This is the longest and most fun day of the trek. You will walk about 8 to 9 kilometers, and it will take around 8 to 9 hours. The route begins with a steady climb to the top of Hampta Pass. As you reach the pass, you’ll see stunning views of the mountains and valleys on both sides. After spending some time at the top, you carefully walk down on the other side to reach Shea Goru. The trail is rocky and slippery, so you need to be careful. Shea Goru is a beautiful and peaceful campsite surrounded by mountains, where you rest for the night.

itinerary.title: Shea goru to Chatru → Drive to Chandratal (if weather permits)
activities: On Day 4, you trek from Shea goru (12,900 ft) to Chatru (11,000 ft), covering around 7 km in 4 to 5 hours. The path goes down and takes you through dry and rocky areas that look like the Spiti region. The views here look very different from the green areas you saw before. After reaching Chatru, if the weather and road conditions are good, you can drive to the beautiful Chandratal Lake (14,000 ft), known for its crescent shape and blue water. The drive takes 2 to 3 hours. You will stay overnight either at Chatru or near Chandratal, depending on the conditions.

itinerary.title: Drive from Chatru/ Chandratal to Manali
activities: On the last day, you will drive back to Manali from Chatru or Chandratal. The distance is around 85 to 100 km and takes about 6 to 7 hours by vehicle. If Rohtang Pass is open, the drive becomes more scenic with amazing mountain views. Enjoy the beautiful landscapes one last time as you return. The journey marks the end of the Hampta Pass trek. You’ll reach Manali by evening with lots of great memories and a sense of achievement.

Blog.title: Chardham Yatra Tour 2025: A Divine Journey to the Abode of Gods
Blog.content:
Overview

The sacred Chardham Yatra is one of the most revered pilgrimage journeys in India. Each year, countless pilgrims embark on a sacred journey to attain blessings and spiritual enlightenment by visiting the four revered shrines of the Garhwal Himalayas — Yamunotri , Gangotri , Kedarnath , and Badrinath.

Our specially designed Chardham Yatra Tour Package would bring all of it with the comfort, convenience and devotion along to make it a great experience for your upcoming year of 2025.

Best Time to Visit Chardham Yatra 2025

  • Opening Dates: May 2025

  • Closing Dates: Late October/Early November 2025

  • Ideal Months: May–June and September–October

  • Avoid: July–August due to heavy monsoon rains and landslides

The Four Sacred Dhams of Chardham Yatra

The Chardham Yatra covers four holy temples in Uttarakhand – Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath. Each of these places is connected with our faith, old stories, and natural beauty. Visiting all four dham is believed to wash away sins and give peace and blessings.

Yamunotri Dham – The Temple of Goddess Yamuna

Yamunotri is the first stop of the Chardham Yatra tour. This temple is dedicated to Goddess Yamuna, the sister of Yama (the God of death). People believe that bathing in the Yamuna water protects us from untimely death and gives purity to the soul. The temple is located at a height of 3,293 meters and is surrounded by beautiful snow mountains and green valleys.


Main attractions at Yamunotri:

  • The journey starts from Hanuman Chatti and a 6 km trek from Janki Chatti takes you to the temple.

  • Pilgrims take a holy dip in Surya Kund, a natural hot water spring near the temple.

  • Devotees offer prayers at Divya Shila, a sacred stone before entering the temple.

Gangotri Dham – The Temple of Goddess Ganga

Gangotri is the second dham of the yatra. It is dedicated to Goddess Ganga, the most sacred river of India. The temple is located at 3,100 meters on the banks of the Bhagirathi River. According to the legend, River Ganga came down to Earth when Lord Shiva released her from his hair locks, after King Bhagirath prayed for the salvation of his ancestors.


Main attractions at Gangotri:

  • The beautiful Gangotri Temple built in white granite.

  • The holy Ganga Aarti performed on the riverbank in the evening.

  • Bhagirath Shila, where King Bhagirath meditated.

  • The scenic Harsil Valley, famous for apple orchards and pine forests.

  • For adventurous devotees, Gaumukh Glacier, the actual source of River Ganga, is an important trek.

Kedarnath Dham – The Temple of Lord Shiva

Kedarnath is the third dham and one of the most popular temples of Lord Shiva. It is also one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. Located at 3,583 meters, the temple stands in the middle of high Himalayan peaks, making it one of the most divine places in India. It is said that the Pandavas came here to ask forgiveness from Lord Shiva after the Mahabharata war.


Main attractions at Kedarnath:

  • The trek to Kedarnath Temple starts from Gaurikund. The trek is about 16 km and is full of natural beauty.

  • Inside the temple, the Shiva Lingam is worshipped as Lord Kedarnath.

  • Bhim Shila, a big rock behind the temple, protected Kedarnath Temple during the flood in 2013.

  • Helicopter services are also available from Phata, Guptkashi, and Dehradun for those who cannot trek.

Badrinath Dham – The Temple of Lord Vishnu

Badrinath is the last dham of the yatra and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. The temple is located at 3,133 meters, on the banks of the Alaknanda River, with the Neelkanth peak in the background. The idol of Lord Vishnu here is in a meditating position, and it is believed that Adi Shankaracharya established this dham in the 8th century.

Main attractions at Badrinath:

  • The hot water spring Tapt Kund, where pilgrims take a bath before darshan.

  • Brahma Kapal, where rituals for ancestors are performed.

  • Nearby holy spots like Narad Kund, Sheshnetra, and Charan Paduka.

  • Mana Village, the last village of India before Tibet.

  • Vyas Gufa, where Sage Vyas wrote the Mahabharata, and Bhim Pul, a natural bridge made by Bhima.

Highlights of the Chardham Yatra Tour Package 2025

1. Embark on a soul-stirring journey through the divine landscapes of Uttarakhand with our thoughtfully crafted Chardham Yatra Tour Packages . Each stop on this sacred route brings spiritual depth, historical importance, and natural beauty. The key highlights of this tour is :

 Begin with blessings at Hanuman Chatti, the starting point for the trek to Yamunotri, known for its serene trails and spiritual energy.

2. Begin a calm and spiritual journey to Yamunotri Temple, the sacred source of the River Yamuna. Surrounded by the beautiful Himalayan mountains, this sacred site offers a truly spiritual experience. Begin your spiritual ritual with a sacred bath in the thermal waters of Surya Kund, known for its purifying properties. Don’t miss offering your prayers at the revered Divya Shila — a sanctified rock located near the temple that holds deep religious significance for devotees.


3. Explore the historic Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Uttarkashi, a sacred shrine devoted to Lord Shiva, and immerse yourself in the serene spiritual energy of this picturesque town set along the banks of the Bhagirathi River.


4. Explore the sacred confluences of Panch Prayag — Devprayag, Rudraprayag, Karnaprayag, Nandprayag, and Vishnuprayag — where holy rivers merge, creating deeply spiritual landscapes.

5. "Start your trek from Gauri Kund, a sacred place where Goddess Parvati is believed to have meditated. From there, move towards the holy Kedarnath Temple , located among the snowy mountains. Don’t miss the Bhim Shila – a huge rock that protected the Kedarnath Temple during the 2013 floods."


6.  Experience the divine ambiance at Badrinath Temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu. En route, visit Brahma Kapal, where rituals for ancestors are performed, and soak in the natural beauty of Sheshnetra, Narad Kund, and Tapt Kund — hot water springs near the temple.


 7. Explore Mana Village, the last Indian village before the Indo-Tibetan border. Visit mystical sites such as Vyas Gufa, where sage Ved Vyas is believed to have composed the Mahabharata, and Bhim Pul, a natural rock bridge associated with Bhima from the Pandavas.

 8. Enjoy the pristine beauty of Harsil Valley, known for its apple orchards, pine forests, and the gurgling Bhagirathi River — a peaceful stop on the way to Gangotri.

A: For the Chardham Yatra, carry warm clothes, comfortable walking shoes, personal medicines, ID proof, toiletries, a raincoat or umbrella, a small backpack, a torch, and a reusable water bottle. Weather can be unpredictable, so pack accordingly.


Q.3. Chardham Yatra suitable for senior citizens?

To ensure their comfort, we provide specially designed packages that include smooth transportation, accessible accommodations, and optional helicopter services to reduce physical exertion and make the pilgrimage more manageable.


Q.4.  Can I personalize the tour package?

A: Yes, we provide customizable Chardham Yatra packages. You can choose your departure city, mode of travel (road/helicopter), preferred hotels, travel dates, and additional sightseeing destinations as per your needs.
